model_annotation:
This plot illustrates training loss curves for different model configurations over the course of training from scratch. The x-axis represents training steps, labeled as "steps," displayed on a linear scale ranging from approximately 0 to 140,000 (with tick marks at 0, 20k, 40k, 60k, 80k, 100k, 120k, and 140k). The y-axis represents loss, displayed on a linear scale ranging from approximately 2 to 14, with tick marks at intervals of 2.

The plot contains several lines corresponding to different methods. A line labeled "Vanilla" (appearing in a dark color, likely black or dark blue) starts at approximately 14 at step 0 and decreases steeply in the early steps, settling to roughly 2.5–3.0 by 140,000 steps. A line for "StrmLLM (n=380)" follows a similar trajectory but appears to plateau at a slightly higher loss value. A line for "StrmLLM (n=256)" shows a comparable decreasing trend but levels off at a noticeably higher loss than the Vanilla line. Lines for "SepLLM (n=64)," "SepLLM (n=128)," "SepLLM (n=64,H)," and "SepLLM (n=64,H/T)" all exhibit steep initial decreases from around 14 and converge to loss values in the range of approximately 2.5–3.5 by 140,000 steps. Among the SepLLM variants, "SepLLM (n=128)" appears to achieve a slightly lower final loss compared to "SepLLM (n=64)," while "SepLLM (n=64,H/T)" also appears to reach a relatively lower loss among the SepLLM configurations. All lines show the steepest decline within the first 20,000 steps, after which the rate of decrease diminishes and the curves gradually flatten toward the end of training.
